Chapter 10: Living in a Holographic Universe
It’s one thing to hear about the holographic model of reality, or to let your mind wander through its possibilities while you’re sipping coffee or relaxing with a good book.
But what if you actually started living as if it were true? Imagine seeing every person you meet, every moment you experience, as a reflection of something much bigger—the whole universe, echoed in each of us.
How would your life change if you really believed that your thoughts, your feelings, and even your smallest actions mattered, not just to you, but to everything and everyone?
For a lot of people, this shift in perspective starts with a single, quiet moment of awareness. Picture a parent, totally swamped by work and family, who suddenly pauses to watch their child sleeping. In that stillness, something stirs—a feeling of connection that goes way beyond words. It’s as if, by caring for this one small life, they’re actually part of something vast and mysterious.
Sometimes, this new way of seeing unfolds during a crisis. Maybe someone’s facing a deep loss, or everything in life feels uncertain. In the middle of that struggle, they discover a strength they never knew they had—a sense of being supported by something larger than themselves. During moments like these, the lines between self and world, between what’s inside and what’s out there, begin to blur.
Living in a holographic universe is about realizing that every action—no matter how tiny—has meaning. It’s about seeing the world, not as a bunch of separate things, but as one living, breathing whole. It’s about honoring the invisible threads that connect you to other people, to the earth, and to the entire cosmos.
Of course, this way of living isn’t always simple. Our world is noisy and full of distractions. It’s easy to slip back into old habits of feeling separate, or wanting to control everything.
But when you hear the stories of people who’ve caught even a glimpse of this deeper reality, it’s a reminder that another way is possible. A way of living that’s grounded in presence, in compassion, and in wonder.
So, what if you carried even a little bit of that awareness into your own day?
